title: The Big Reveal
subtitle: Imagine It. Build It. Play It.

scenes.name: The hook
scenes.visual: Deep forest-green void. A face-down card drifts out of the dark, turns toward camera and flips to reveal 1 / One. A second card glides in from the right and flips: another 1. They slide together, turn green and pulse. Tiny flat sparks burst out. Kinetic type: 'GAME CREATOR'.
scenes.camera: Slow push-in (scale 1.0 to 1.08). Background cards move on three parallax layers.
scenes.sfx: Low ambient swell, soft whoosh on the entrance, card flip ×2, match chime, sparkle.
scenes.music: Ambient pad only. The music bed starts under line h3.
scenes.transition: The matched pair flies up into the game grid (match cut).

lines.text: Have you ever played a game that made you think, remember and smile every time you got a match?
Well, what if I told you that you could build a game like that yourself?
Yes! You are about to become a game creator.

scenes.name: What you will build
scenes.visual: The real finished Number Match page (flat redesign) on a tilted browser that settles flat. A cursor plays: one match, one miss, then a fast-forward to the win. Moves, timer and progress update live. The win overlay appears.
scenes.camera: 3D tilt (rotateX 18° to 0°) with a slow zoom. Push-in on the stats when they change.
scenes.sfx: Click + flip on every card, match chime, gentle mismatch, three-note win tune (the game's own notes: 660/830/990 Hz).
scenes.music: Bed at full, ducked under the voice.
scenes.transition: Whip pan left to the three language labels.

lines.text: Together, we are going to build Number Match: a fun memory game where you turn over cards, find matching numbers and challenge your memory.
And the most exciting part? You will create it yourself, one step at a time!

scenes.name: HTML, CSS, JavaScript
scenes.visual: Three large tiles drop in when each word is spoken. HTML (red): wireframe boxes stack up. CSS (green): a grey box becomes the red number card. JAVASCRIPT (gold): the card flips by itself.
scenes.camera: Locked. Each tile pops forward when it is named.
scenes.onScreen: HTML: BUILD THE STRUCTURE · CSS: MAKE IT BEAUTIFUL · JAVASCRIPT: BRING IT TO LIFE
scenes.sfx: A distinct pop for each tile (low, mid, high), whoosh out.
scenes.transition: The tiles shrink into the three files in the IDE sidebar.

lines.text: We will start with HTML, the language that gives our game its structure.
Then we will use CSS to make our cards colourful, beautiful and exciting.
Finally, we will use JavaScript to make everything work.

scenes.name: Paisley Studio
scenes.visual: The Paisley IDE, recreated from the screenshots, slides up: top bar with the 'Paisley VS Code' pill, Save and Run; sidebar with new-file, new-folder and upload; editor; preview; console bar. Rings highlight the sidebar, the editor and the preview in turn. A cursor clicks into the editor and the first lines of index.html type in. Run is clicked and the preview shows the game.
scenes.camera: Slow push toward the editor while the code types.
scenes.music: Bed ducked, then lifts on i3.
scenes.transition: The preview zooms to fill the frame, then dissolves to the title card.

lines.text: And guess where we will build everything? Right here, inside the Paisley Studio coding environment.
Get ready, because you are not just going to play a game.
You are going to create one!

scenes.name: Title and branding
scenes.visual: Deep green. The Number Match logotype builds (red N tile, NUMBER in white, MATCH in red), cards fan out behind it, then the Paisley Studio badge and the line 'Imagine it. Build it. Play it.' Next lesson tag: 'Next: HTML: Building the Foundation'.
scenes.onScreen: NUMBER MATCH · Imagine it. Build it. Play it. · Next: HTML: Building the Foundation
